flags.item: The three submitted identifiers are not 10-character ASINs
flags.detail: The identifiers in the submitted links are B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV. Each is 9 characters long. The official Creators API documentation shows ASIN examples of 10 characters (S06), and all three redirect targets use 10-character IDs (S14-S16). Typing amazon.com/dp/<each ID> returns 'Page Not Found' (S08-S10). No product name, brand, price, rating or commission can be tied to these identifiers. Confirmed by the GetItems reference (S06, chunk 1 of 3): an ASIN is a 10-character identifier.
flags.action: Provide the intended product page URL or 10-character ASIN for each product (the owner's input is needed; this session cannot infer it).

flags.item: Short links redirect to three different products, not confirmed as the submitted products
flags.detail: Each short link ended on a different amazon.com product page (S11-S13), and the mapping was the same on two fetches each. The final URLs carry the parameters lv=shuf and plpRedirect=mhFallback. The page titles identify two CHEFMAN air fryers and one Emeril Lagasse air fryer toaster oven (S14-S16). What these parameters mean is not documented in any official source reviewed, so they are recorded as observed only and never used as product data. The direct amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH request returns a 'Continue shopping' interstitial (S16), so product 3's title is only readable through the short link (S23).

The short links redirected automatically to amazon.com in the fetch tool (S11-S13). A third-party competitor claims link.amazon forwards to amzlinks.in (S17). That claim is not verified against any Amazon page.
flags.action: Test each link while logged in to an Associates account and record whether tracked clicks appear. Generate Special Links from Associates Central instead, if the owner wants to use them.

flags.item: The AI analysis layer cannot use Creators API data without written approval
flags.detail: Creators API terms bar aggregating, analysing or repurposing Product Advertising Content without express prior written approval, and bar using Program Content to develop or train machine learning or language models (PF-23, PF-24, PF-25). The brief asks for an AI-powered platform. Any AI analysis of Amazon data is therefore blocked until approval is obtained. No AI analysis of Amazon data has been built. Widened 2026-11-14 (session ecbfe91b, adopting c4e71983-FLG-16): the bar is not limited to Creators API data. Program Policies, Participation Requirements section 5, reads verbatim: “You will not, without or express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology.” (S02; re-read live 2026-11-14; the odd wording ‘without or express’ is Amazon’s own text, reproduced verbatim.) Any machine-learning use of Special Links or Program Content needs Amazon’s express prior written approval — not only Creators API data.
flags.action: Owner: request written approval from Amazon for the planned analysis before building it, or limit the analysis to data the site already displays.

Requirement 6(y): the site must not have price tracking or price-alert functionality. Commission Income Statement 2(e): a purchase referred by a 'Redirecting Link' (one that sends users indirectly through an intermediate site without a click on that site) is disqualified. The submitted links are short links that land on other product pages (S11-S13). Their use on this site has not been checked against 2(e).
